Bassline (music genre) | Bassline (sometimes referred to as bassline house, Niche or 4x4) is a type of music related to UK garage that originated in Sheffield in the early 2000s.  Stylistically it comprises a four-to-the-floor rhythm normally at around 135–142 beats per minute, a strong emphasis on bass, and a pop music aesthetic similar to that of its precursor 2-step garage.
Do You Think About Me | "Do You Think About Me" is a song recorded by 50 Cent for his fourth studio album, "Before I Self Destruct".  The song was released as the second official single from the album on January 16, 2010, and released in the UK on March 22, 2010.  The song is produced by Rockwilder & Chris N Teeb and features uncredited vocals from R&B singer and G-Unit/G-Note artist Governor.
I Love You 'Cause I Have To | "I Love You 'Cause I Have To" is a pop rock song by British band Dogs Die in Hot Cars.  It was their debut single on label Radiate, released alongside "Celebrity Sanctum" and "Somewhat Off The Way."  The three-track release peaked at number 79 on the UK Singles Chart.  Described as "mix of ska rhythms and new wave pop hooks" by Allmusic, "I Love You 'Cause I Have To" gained enough critical and commercial success to gain a recording contract with V2 Records, who released their debut album, "Please Describe Yourself".  The song was the second single from the album, released in both the UK and international territories.  "I Love You 'Cause I Have To"'s main release debuted and peaked on the UK Singles Chart at number 32 on the week of 17 July 2004, before dropping to number 67 the following week, then exiting the Top 100.  The song was written by band member Craig Macintosh, and produced by Clive Langer and Alan Winstanley, who also produced "Please Describe Yourself".
I Think I'm in Love with You | "I Think I'm in Love with You" is a song written and produced by Cory Rooney and Dan Shea for Jessica Simpson's debut album "Sweet Kisses" (1999).  It contains a sample of singer-songwriter John Mellencamp's "Jack & Diane" (1982) and was released as the album's third and final single in summer 2000 (see 2000 in music).  The song's protagonist declares "Boy I think that I'm in love with you, got me doin' silly things when it comes to you".  The single reached at top ten in Australia, Canada and Japan and in the top 20 in Canada, the UK, Scotland and New Zealand.  In the United States, it reached #21.
Think About You (song) | "Think About You" is a song by American recording R&B artist Luther Vandross.  The song is from Luther Vandross' 2003 album, "Dance with My Father".  "Think About You" was minor hit after its release, and would later peak to #30 on "Billboard's" Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart.
You Don't Love Me (Willie Cobbs song) | "You Don't Love Me" is a rhythm and blues-influenced blues song recorded by American musician Willie Cobbs in 1960.  It is Cobbs' best-known song and features a guitar figure and melody that has appealed to musicians in several genres.  Although it became a regional hit when it was released in Memphis, Tennessee, copyright issues prevented its further promotion and national chart success.  Derived from an earlier song by Bo Diddley, it has inspired many popular adaptations, including "Shimmy Shimmy Walk" by the Megatons and "You Don't Love Me (No, No, No)" by Jamaican singer Dawn Penn.

Think About You (song) | "Think About You" is a song by American recording R&B artist Luther Vandross.  The song is from Luther Vandross' 2003 album, "Dance with My Father".  "Think About You" was minor hit after its release, and would later peak to #30 on "Billboard's" Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart.
You Don't Love Me (Willie Cobbs song) | "You Don't Love Me" is a rhythm and blues-influenced blues song recorded by American musician Willie Cobbs in 1960. What's It Gonna Be (H "Two" O song) | "What's It Gonna Be?"  is a bassline (subgenre of UK garage) song performed by the duo known as H "Two" O (Selim Ben Rabha, "Solution", and Simon McDevitt, "Oz", who also go by "Hit 'Em" and "Hard") and the British three-person bassline vocal group Platnum (Aaron Evers, Mina Poli, and Michelle McKenna). Platnum | Platnum are a British bassline vocal group from Manchester, England, consisting of male vocalist Aaron Evers and female vocalists Mina Poli and Michelle McKenna. Bassline Junkie | "Bassline Junkie" is a song by British rapper Dizzee Rascal from his mixtape "Dirtee TV.com – The Mixtape EP, Vol.2" (2013).  The song was produced by M. J. What Kind of Fool Do You Think I Am | "What Kind of Fool Do You Think I Am" is a song recorded by American country music artist Lee Roy Parnell, written by Al Carmichael and Gary Griffin. What Do You Know About Love | "What Do You Know About Love" is a song written and recorded by American country music artist Dwight Yoakam. I Think About You | I Think About You is the fourth studio album released by American country music artist Collin Raye. What Were We Thinking Of | "What Were We Thinking Of" is a song recorded by American singer Barbra Streisand for her twenty-ninth studio album, "Till I Loved You" (1988). Do You Love What You Feel | "Do You Love What You Feel" is a well-known soul/disco song by Rufus and Chaka. What Do You Think About the Car? | What Do You Think About the Car?  is the debut studio album by English singer-songwriter and musician Declan McKenna.  It was released worldwide on 21 July 2017, through Columbia Records.
Something About You (New Edition song) | "Something About You" is the fourth single by New Edition from their album Home Again, prominently sampling Edie Brickell's track "What I Am". Baby, What About You | "Baby, What About You" is a song written by Josh Leo and Wendy Waldman, and recorded by American country music artist Crystal Gayle.
